## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. From the code: observations are [B, 4Z+3, Y, X] and include ready-made missing, extra and height channels. Actions are n_types×Y×X anchors (top-left) plus DONE, so the existing footprint pooling matches the action layout. Locally, the network can tell whether a placement is good: the brick lands at the highest point under its footprint, and every cell it fills at that layer should be missing. So the zero score probably comes from too few samples (only 32 updates) and an unsharp greedy policy, not from missing receptive field. This round goes after any nonzero success: (1) the recipe alone, with 1 PPO epoch for about 3.25× more samples, higher gamma and lambda, and lower entropy; (2) the same recipe plus a normalised residual trunk with a wider per-column MLP; (3) the same recipe plus a new head that scores each placement layer by layer.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored exactly 0 on dev and 0 on training success, on both seeds. Changing the recipe (1 epoch, about 400k steps), adding normalisation and residual blocks, and using per-layer slices all failed to give any successful episode. This does not look like seed noise. I see three possible causes: (1) the placement head cannot score whole footprints; (2) there are too few or too noisy gradient updates; (3) the world differs from its description in some way I can't observe. In the baseline head, each cell is projected separately and then pooled with max, min and mean. That loses which cell is which inside the footprint, but a placement is valid only if every footprint cell is missing at the shared landing layer. A learned convolution whose kernel matches each footprint's (dy,dx) shape would see each footprint cell separately at the same compute. So I test that head alone, the recipe alone, and the two together.

### Round 3
After six trials, every result is still 0. That covers both seeds, both dev and training success, at 230k–405k steps, across four architectures and two recipes. Not one exact build appeared even during stochastic training. Seed noise can't explain six straight zeros, so the spatial heads probably share a systematic problem rather than just learning slowly. All six trials score cell (y,x) only from features at or near (y,x), and they assume actions are laid out as type × y × x. The task says the world may differ from its description. If the action order differs (x and y swapped, cell-major instead of type-major, or another anchor convention), every local head is pointing at the wrong cells, and recipe changes can't fix that. So this round tests heads that don't depend on the action layout: a learned flat head added to the conv head, a conv encoder with only a flat head, and a pure MLP. If training success becomes nonzero, a layout mismatch is the likely cause.

### Round 4
All nine trials score 0 on dev and 0 on training success, on both seeds. This holds for spatial heads (pooling, footprint-kernel, per-layer), for flat heads and for a pure MLP, and for recipes with 1 or 2 epochs and small or large minibatches. The flat and pure-MLP trials also failing makes an action-layout mismatch unlikely as the only cause. The more likely bottleneck is sample efficiency on a hard exact-match task, together with weak relational reasoning and DONE timing. No configuration differs from another beyond noise, so there is nothing reliable to refine. In this last round I try three different ways to get any nonzero success:
- a deeper residual trunk with a footprint head that also reads the legality mask;
- an aggressive, sharper recipe on the baseline network with many small updates and a long horizon;
- a small transformer over cells, whose global receptive field could help the network judge whether a placement is supported and when to call DONE.
